incident.title: Storefront 5xx alert firing
symptoms: storefront 5xx rate above 18% since about 18:21 UTC
Add-to-cart and cart totals are failing; browsing works
The alert has not cleared after 30 minutes

tasks.goal: Find out which endpoints and which upstream calls the 5xx errors come from in storefront logs and metrics. Check whether the errors are limited to the add-to-cart and cart-total paths while browse paths stay healthy. Find the exact onset time near 18:21 UTC.

params.focus: 5xx rate by endpoint, upstream error codes, timeouts, latency

tasks.goal: List deploys, config changes, feature-flag flips and infrastructure changes to storefront and its cart, pricing and checkout dependencies shortly before or near 18:21 UTC.

Map the dependencies on the storefront add-to-cart and cart-total paths, such as the cart service, pricing, promotions and session/cache stores. Separate them from dependencies used only by browsing. Find past incidents where cart failed while browsing still worked.

Combine the error breakdown, the change timeline and the dependency map into competing, ranked root-cause hypotheses for the cart-only 5xx errors that started near 18:21 UTC. For each hypothesis, give the supporting and contradicting evidence and the next checks or mitigation.

Establish causal direction. Pull pricing-svc CPU, replica count, p99 latency, error rate and inbound rps, plus promo-db query latency, connections and errors, at the finest resolution available. Determine whether pricing-svc or promo-db degradation began before or after cart-svc outbound_pricing_rps started rising between 18:15Z and 18:25Z. Also pull pricing-svc ERROR logs.

Measure cart-svc amplification and its source. Pull cart-svc requests_per_s by endpoint and caller, outbound_pricing_rps, retry and timeout counters, and pricing calls per request over time, especially 18:00Z (before the deploy), 18:10Z and 18:15Z. Also pull storefront-to-cart-svc call rate by storefront endpoint, including the home page and carousel, before and after the 18:05Z v12.3.0 deploy. Goal: decide whether the 18x rise is a retry loop, per-item fan-out, or new carousel-driven traffic.

Close gap:2. Retry the storefront log query for 18:15-18:35Z at ERROR and WARN levels, group 5xx by endpoint and upstream target, and reconcile the counts with the 18.6% error rate at 810 rps. Confirm that browse and catalog-svc endpoints are clean and whether any home-page or carousel requests fail or call cart-svc.

Revise the hypotheses with the new findings. The Critic said: h1 rests mostly on two samples: outbound pricing traffic of 420 rps at 18:15Z and 7650 rps at 18:25Z, against one inbound reading of 455 rps at 18:25Z. Four problems weaken it.

(1) The baseline pricing-calls-per-request ratio is inferred, not measured. cart-svc inbound rps at 18:15Z and earlier was never pulled, so we do not know whether inbound traffic stayed flat or shifted in mix after the 18:05Z storefront deploy.

(2) An 18x amplification does not fit a plain retry storm. The only retry evidence is 'timed out after 3 attempts', and that is storefront retrying cart-svc, not cart-svc retrying pricing-svc. Retries would give roughly 3-4x at most. 18x points to per-item fan-out, such as per-product price lookups, or a retry loop with no cap. Per-product price lookups fit h3: the carousel could hit a cart or price endpoint that fans out per product. So h3 should not be marked contradicted by cartin:0001 until the cart-svc inbound mix by endpoint and caller is compared before and after 18:05Z.

(3) There is no pricing-svc or promo-db data at all. h2 and h4 both say the pricing slowdown came first and the spike is a response to it. Neither has been tested, so causal direction is unresolved. h4 at 0.0 confidence is unjustified, since nothing contradicts it except the spike that it would itself explain.

(4) gap:2 hides the bulk of the storefront errors: only 2 ERROR lines came back against about 150 failing requests per second. 'Cart paths only' and 'cart-svc is the sole upstream' are therefore unverified.

The ranking could flip between h1, h2/h4 and h3 depending on the onset order of pricing latency versus the cart-svc fan-out, and on whether the carousel generates the extra cart-svc traffic.

Pin the onset of the pricing load surge relative to the 18:05Z storefront deploy and the 18:20:05Z promo-db failover log, and establish the baseline pricing-calls-per-request ratio.

Query at 1-minute resolution:
1. cart-svc outbound_pricing_rps
2. cart-svc requests_per_s
3. pricing-svc cpu_pct

Report the first minute each series diverges from baseline, and the outbound/inbound ratio at 18:00Z, 18:10Z and 18:15Z.

If one call remains, pull promo-db logs or events (failover, leader election) for 18:00Z-18:25Z to confirm the failover's start and end.

Revise the hypotheses with the new findings. The Critic said: h4 (promo-db failover as trigger) ranks first, but it rests on one pricing-svc log line at 18:20:05Z. There is no promo-db event record, and the only promo-db sample is CPU 22% at 18:25Z. That sample is neutral rather than contradicting, since a failover could already have finished by then.

The bigger problem is that h4 does not explain why the alert has not cleared after 30+ minutes. A failover is transient. The persistence comes from something that sustains the overload. The candidate is cart-svc retries with max_attempts=5, backoff=0ms and jitter off (h1). So h4 and h1 are not competing: one is the trigger and the other keeps the overload going. The ranking should treat h4 as trigger and h1 as amplifier/root, not as alternatives.

The outbound pricing call ratio is about 16.8 per cart-svc request (7650/455). That is more than 5 retries can produce, so per-item fan-out must be part of the load. The source of that extra load is still unresolved. The cart-svc inbound rate at 18:15Z was never retrieved, so the baseline ratio is unknown. The deploys query found no deploy or config change for cart-svc, pricing-svc or promo-db, but it cannot show feature-flag flips.

h3 (storefront v12.3.0 carousel at 18:05Z) has not been ruled out. With samples 10 minutes apart, the outbound rise could have started at any time between 18:15Z and 18:25Z, and 420 rps at 18:15Z may already be part of it.

One measurement decides between trigger-first (h4/h1) and load-first (h3): when cart-svc outbound_pricing_rps and pricing-svc CPU first diverge, compared with 18:05Z and 18:20:05Z, plus cart-svc inbound rps for the baseline ratio. Only 4 tool calls remain, so I am requesting a single focused investigation. The promo-db event check is included as a lower-priority item in the same task.

Storefront requests_per_s was 810.0 at 18:25Z.

cart-svc outbound_pricing_rps rose from 420.0 at 18:15Z to 7650.0 at 18:25Z, while cart-svc requests_per_s was 455.0 at 18:25Z.

cart-svc requests_per_s (inbound) was 455.0 at 18:25:00Z.

At 18:25:00Z, cart-svc made about 16.8 outbound pricing calls per inbound request (7650 / 455), computed from the two cited values. The two samples are at the same timestamp, so this is a rough ratio.
Storefront error_rate_pct rose from 0.4% at 18:15:00Z to 18.6% at 18:25:00Z.
Storefront requests_per_s was 810.0 at 18:25:00Z.
Storefront deployed v12.3.0 at 18:05:00Z, described as 'New product carousel on the home page'. No other deploys or config changes appear for any service in 17:50Z–18:40Z.
cart-svc logged 'pricing-svc call failed (503)' at 18:20:06Z for retry 1/5 and retry 5/5. The client is configured with max_attempts=5, backoff=0ms, and jitter=off.

assumptions.statement: The retry policy (max_attempts=5, no backoff, no jitter) is contributing to pricing-svc load. Retries against a failing pricing-svc would then cause immediate, synchronized re-attempts.
assumptions.basis: Log lines at 18:20:06Z show retries reaching 5/5 with backoff=0ms and jitter=off.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Pull pricing-svc inbound rps and 503 rate over 18:00Z–18:30Z, and cart-svc retry counters, to confirm retries are a large share of the 7650 rps.

assumptions.statement: Retries alone cannot explain the ~17x pricing-call-per-request ratio, because max_attempts=5 caps pricing calls per logical pricing call at 5. A per-item fan-out (one pricing call per cart or carousel item) must be multiplying the load, with retries as a secondary amplifier.
assumptions.basis: Arithmetic from the cited values: 7650/455 ≈ 16.8 outbound calls per inbound request, versus a retry cap of 5 attempts per call.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Get cart-svc outbound pricing calls per request and items per request (by endpoint and caller) for 18:00Z, 18:10Z and 18:15Z. A rising items-per-cart ratio confirms fan-out.

assumptions.basis: The deploy at 18:05:00Z is the only change in the window and is described as a home-page carousel. The outbound rise (420 at 18:15Z to 7650 at 18:25Z) follows it. The 18:00Z and 18:10Z points are missing, so the onset cannot be pinned.

Outbound pricing calls went from 420 to 7650 rps and pricing-svc CPU from 34% to 99%. Storefront errors were still present at 18:35:44Z, and storefront's own 3 attempts against cart-svc add to the load. Retries alone cap at 5x per logical call, but the observed ratio is about 16.8 calls per inbound request. critic_reviews.critique:
h1 rests mostly on two samples: outbound pricing traffic of 420 rps at 18:15Z and 7650 rps at 18:25Z, against one inbound reading of 455 rps at 18:25Z. Four problems weaken it.

(1) The baseline pricing-calls-per-request ratio is inferred, not measured. cart-svc inbound rps at 18:15Z and earlier was never pulled, so we do not know whether inbound traffic stayed flat or shifted in mix after the 18:05Z storefront deploy.

(2) An 18x amplification does not fit a plain retry storm. The only retry evidence is 'timed out after 3 attempts', and that is storefront retrying cart-svc, not cart-svc retrying pricing-svc. Retries would give roughly 3-4x at most. 18x points to per-item fan-out, such as per-product price lookups, or a retry loop with no cap. Per-product price lookups fit h3: the carousel could hit a cart or price endpoint that fans out per product. So h3 should not be marked contradicted by cartin:0001 until the cart-svc inbound mix by endpoint and caller is compared before and after 18:05Z.

(3) There is no pricing-svc or promo-db data at all. h2 and h4 both say the pricing slowdown came first and the spike is a response to it. Neither has been tested, so causal direction is unresolved. h4 at 0.0 confidence is unjustified, since nothing contradicts it except the spike that it would itself explain.

(4) gap:2 hides the bulk of the storefront errors: only 2 ERROR lines came back against about 150 failing requests per second. 'Cart paths only' and 'cart-svc is the sole upstream' are therefore unverified.

The ranking could flip between h1, h2/h4 and h3 depending on the onset order of pricing latency versus the cart-svc fan-out, and on whether the carousel generates the extra cart-svc traffic.

recommended_actions.action: Reduce the cart-svc to pricing-svc retry policy from max_attempts=5 with 0ms backoff and no jitter to a single retry with exponential backoff and jitter, and recommend deploying it to cart-svc as soon as it can be validated.
recommended_actions.rationale: Immediate retries against an already-saturated pricing-svc are the feedback loop that keeps its CPU at 99% and the alert active. Cutting retries removes the self-sustaining load even if the original trigger has passed.

recommended_actions.action: Recommend adding a circuit breaker on cart-svc calls to pricing-svc so that, once failures cross a threshold, cart-svc fails fast or serves a degraded cart total instead of sending more load.
recommended_actions.rationale: A breaker lets pricing-svc recover without requiring every retry to be stopped by hand, and limits the storefront 5xx impact of any future dependency blip.

recommended_actions.action: Recommend pulling baseline per-request pricing call ratios and cart-svc retry counters for 17:30Z to 18:30Z to quantify how much of the roughly 16.8 calls per inbound request retries account for, versus per-item fan-out.
recommended_actions.rationale: The retry cap of 5 cannot explain a 16.8x ratio alone, so the retry contribution is unquantified. This measurement determines how much weight h1 and the fan-out hypotheses should carry in the final root cause.

recommended_actions.action: Recommend pulling 1-minute series for cart-svc outbound_pricing_rps, pricing-svc cpu_pct, and storefront inbound rps from 18:00Z to 18:30Z, to check whether the rise in pricing calls begins before the 18:20:05Z promo-db error.
recommended_actions.rationale: This is the deciding check for h3. A divergence before 18:20:05Z would support the carousel fan-out as the load source. A divergence only after it would weaken h3.

recommended_actions.action: If the 1-minute series show pricing fan-out starting before 18:20:05Z, recommend disabling the home-page product carousel in storefront v12.3.0 as a fast mitigation, with a full rollback to the prior version as the fallback.
recommended_actions.rationale: The carousel is the only recorded change in the window and could drive per-product pricing lookups. Turning it off is faster and more reversible than a rollback, and it is only justified if the timing check supports h3.

recommended_actions.action: Recommend pulling promo-db failover and leader-election events from 18:00Z to 18:25Z to confirm the trigger timing and duration.
recommended_actions.rationale: The only support for h4 is one pricing-svc log line, and no failover record exists in the data. Confirming the event anchors the trigger and checks whether the failover finished before the storm started.

recommended_actions.action: Recommend auditing the feature-flag change log for cart-svc and pricing-svc from 17:30Z to 19:00Z, looking for per-item price or promotion evaluation flags.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploys query cannot show flag changes, so a flip could be the source of the per-item fan-out and would not appear in existing evidence. The audit either finds it or rules it out.

recommended_actions.action: Recommend scaling pricing-svc out horizontally as temporary capacity relief while the retry and circuit-breaker changes are made.
recommended_actions.rationale: Added capacity gives pricing-svc headroom to recover from saturation. It does not address the retry loop or the fan-out source, so it should be paired with the h1 changes rather than used alone.
